description: This topic helps in understanding the comparative relationship between two or more quantities. A ratio is a comparison by division, while a proportion represents the equality of two ratios.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles of Ratio and Proportion.

key_concepts.explanation: It is a relationship between two homogeneous quantities showing how many times one quantity is of the other. The term 'a' is called the antecedent and 'b' is called the consequent.
When two ratios are equal, they are said to be in proportion. In this case, the product of extremes is equal to the product of means, which means a × d = b × c.
When one quantity increases and the other quantity decreases in the exact same ratio, the relationship between them is called inversely proportional.

sections.title: Important Formulas and Theorems
sections.description: Mathematical formulas related to various types of proportions and theorems.

sections.title: Important Properties of Ratio
sections.description: Classification of various forms of ratios and their mathematical properties.

key_concepts.explanation: The ratio obtained by squaring the terms of a given ratio.
The ratio obtained by extracting the square root of the terms of a given ratio.
The ratio of the product of antecedents to the product of consequents of two or more given ratios.

sections.title: Problem Solving Strategies
sections.description: Step-by-step approach to solve various types of numerical questions efficiently.

steps.title: Combining Ratios
steps.detail: If a:b and b:c are given, to find a:b:c, use the inverse 'N' method or the empty space method: multiply vertically and diagonally as a×b : b×b : b×c.

steps.title: Division of Amount
steps.detail: To divide a total amount in the ratio a:b:c, first find the proportional sum (a+b+c), then calculate the value of each share by multiplying the fraction (a / (a+b+c)) by the Total amount.

steps.title: Coins based Problems
steps.detail: Multiply the number of coins by their face value to find the ratio of their total values. Then, equate the sum of these ratio units to the total amount given in the question to find the multiplier.

sections.title: Common Cases and Applications
sections.description: Special cases frequently asked in competitive scenarios and their quick results.

results: If the income and expenditure ratios of two individuals are given and their savings are equal, use the cross-multiplication method directly to find the value of one proportional unit.

cases.condition: Adding or Removing Liquids in a Mixture
results: If the initial ratio of milk and water is given and only water is added, balance the ratios by equating the quantity of milk in both the initial and final ratios.
Establish a direct relation between the total mixture volume and the proportional sum to find the value of the added quantity.
